data.narrative:
Gilmour Space Technologies, an Australian Space & Aerospace company at Series D having raised approximately $100M to date, is valued here against a peer universe of 5 public comparables (RKLB, PL, LUNR, ASTS, SATL) and 8 private-stage peers including Apex Space, Varda Space Industries, and Skyryse.

Two valuation methods triangulate meaningfully. Stage-progression analysis applies a 1.5x step-up multiplier typical of Series D advancement to the $100M raised proxy, implying $150M. Peer-median anchoring across four same-sector, same/adjacent-stage companies—Apex Space ($2.3B Series D), Varda Space Industries ($1.6B Series D), Sierra Space ($8.0B Series C), and Skyryse ($1.1B Series C)—yields a median of $1.9B, with a range spanning $1.1B to $8.0B. Public-comparable P/S analysis cannot be applied absent disclosed revenue for the target. The wide dispersion among private peers reflects heterogeneity in maturity and market position within the sector.

The triangulated analysis supports a valuation range of $128M (low) to $2.2B (high), with a median of $1.0B. Key uncertainties include Gilmour's revenue trajectory, market traction relative to better-capitalized peers, and the timing to next funding event. The peer-median method carries greater weight given relevance to stage and sector, though the high bound remains sensitive to outlier valuations in this nascent, capital-intensive sector.
